The three streaming options for presentation-based tracks in the 'Designing Hybrid Conference Experiences' guide are:

- Option #1: Single camera pointed at stage, onsite presenter, and slides. Presenters use their own laptop. (Disadvantage: remote attendees may struggle to read slides.)
- Option #2: Single conference laptop used by all onsite presenters. Join the meeting from that laptop; no extra camera; slides + video shared in good quality. Requires collecting presentations in advance.
- Option #3: All presenters log into meeting and share via screen sharing while projecting to room. Streaming laptop + projector + mic. Works for onsite/remote; needs stable net; lag possible.

How Option #2 enhances remote presentation quality: By using one conference laptop for all onsite presenters, you join the online meeting from that laptop without needing an additional camera, and both the speaker video and the slides are shared natively within the online meeting system in good quality. This yields 'high quality of both speaker and presentation stream' and makes remote presentations possible, avoiding the poor slide readability of Option #1 and the lag risks of Option #3.

Option #2 description states: "You can rely on a single conference laptop which must be used by all onsite presenters. - "high quality of both speaker and presentation stream"
- "remote presentations possible"
By using one laptop for all, both speaker video (via webcam) and slides are shared natively in the meeting system at good quality, avoiding the poor slide readability of Option #1 and the lag risks of Option #3. Clear early communication of deadlines is key to enabling this quality.

**Presentation-based tracks – streaming options (from Section 1: Technical Setup):**
For presentation-based tracks (e.g., paper presentations), a lightweight streaming approach using an online meeting system (e.g., Zoom) is recommended. There are three possible streaming options, minimalistic in hardware (only webcam + common AV: mic, projection, network):

- **Option #1:** Single camera pointed at stage, onsite presenter, and slides. Presenters use own laptop. Disadvantage: remote attendees may struggle to read slides; needs camera fed to streaming PC.
- **Option #2:** Single conference laptop used by all onsite presenters. Join meeting from that laptop; no extra camera; slides + video shared in good quality. Requires collecting presentations in advance.
- **Option #3:** All presenters log into meeting and share via screen sharing while projecting to room. Streaming laptop + projector + mic. Works for onsite/remote; needs stable net; lag possible.

**How Option #2 enhances remote presentation quality:**
Option #2 description states: "You can rely on a single conference laptop which must be used by all onsite presenters. The advantage is that you can join the online meeting system from that laptop, you do not need an additional camera, and both videos and slides can be shared within the online meeting system in good quality."
Its listed Pros explicitly show enhancement for remote quality:
- "high quality of both speaker and presentation stream"
- "remote presentations possible"
By using one laptop for all, both speaker video (via webcam) and slides are shared natively in the meeting system at good quality, avoiding the poor slide readability of Option #1 and the lag risks of Option #3. Clear early communication of deadlines is key to enabling this quality.
